# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-19

**The Indonesia long-form, now titled “Why Ravana Gets His Powers From ALLAH in This Ramayana”, has 44,132 views in 43 hours. Its subscribers reach the data in two or three days. The free slot goes to a follow-up long-form for its viewers. The Tipu Short is due tomorrow and nothing is scripted.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script, record and publish one Tipu Sultan Short on the fall of Srirangapatna in 1799: who took the treasure, and who wrote his story afterwards.** (short, due 2026-11-20, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Due tomorrow and no script is on disk. It is the owner's pick of 15 November: the prize money and palace treasure taken on 4 May 1799, then the British writing of Tipu as a tyrant. The Karnataka row over his legacy has dropped out of this week's news, so the Short stands on the story and the searched name, not on a news peg.  
   First step: Script and record today. Sentence one is one sum or one object from the prize records, checked against the original. Put “Tipu Sultan” first in the title. Publish 20 November before 18:00 IST.
2. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: The top-ranked date of the next three weeks, and it sits with Aurangzeb, the subject of the channel's two largest videos. Videos that size brought 66.3% of lifetime subscribers, and this month none has come: 0 against 1,226 planned. It rests on the date and the name, not on proof.  
   First step: Script on disk by 21 November: sentence one is the order, the place and the date, told as an act of state, not a martyrdom story. Record on 22 November, publish the evening of 23 November.
3. **Script and publish a follow-up long-form for the Indonesia video's viewers: why Bali stayed Hindu when Java converted.** (long, due 2026-12-02, new)  
   Why: The Indonesia long-form has 44,132 views in 43 hours, and a video that keeps climbing is the moment to give its viewers the next one, before it cools. Its comments come from Indonesia and Java. The topic is a guess from those comments; the video's subscribers reach the data around 22 November.  
   First step: After the Tipu Short, list sources on Majapahit's fall and who moved to Bali. On 22 November, drop this if the Indonesia video brings fewer subscribers per 1,000 views than the Asia long-form.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
17,800 subscribers against 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 19,286, which needs 58.9 net a day; the 7-day rate is 80.1 and the 28-day rate 40.4. Projection basis: 7-day rate, which ends the month at 18,682, 604 short, and the channel is 790 behind the ramp today. The 7-day rate rests on the film weeks, and uploads account for only 42.2% of net subscribers over 28 days, so the rate rests on growth outside the videos that can stop without warning. The lever furthest behind is breakouts: 0 subscribers against 1,226 planned this month, and the Indonesia long-form is the video to watch for one. The owner dropped the Ravana fact-check long-form on 18 November; its slot goes to the Indonesia follow-up. None of last week's five Shorts came from the brief's list; the two that beat the usual were both about Ravana, and the Indonesia long-form now carries Ravana in its title too. Analytics runs to 2026-11-16, the day before that launch: long-form did 46,205 views in those 7 days, down 38.1% on the week before.

What's working
- “Why Ravana Gets His Powers From ALLAH in This Ramayana” runs at 1,024.8 views an hour; the Asia long-form has averaged 323.2 an hour over its life. Its like rate is 1.7% against 0.9% for the Asia one. It now carries the title that says what was done to Ravana, not the search-led one. Judge it on day three, 20 November, and on subscribers when they arrive.
- Long-form still brings most of the subscribers that uploads bring: 70.9% of upload-attributed net subscribers over 28 days, on 37.7% of upload views. That is why the free slot goes to a long-form.
- The best converter in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 12.2 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the shape for the Bali script's ending: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”

What's wrong
- Neither open Short has a script on disk. Tipu is due tomorrow and lapses on 23 November if it does not ship, and the Tegh Bahadur script was due on disk today. Probable cause: the Indonesia launch took the week. Test: none. If the week holds only one Short, make Tegh Bahadur, the higher-ranked date, and mark Tipu dropped so the list stays honest.
- Film reach is still not turning into subscribers: “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita” brings 0.2 net subscribers per 1,000 views and the Asia long-form 2. Long-form's rate over the 365-day window has fallen out of its usual range to 8.3, and only 41.5% of November's long-form views were engaged views, so part of the fall is how views are counted since August. Probable cause: the film videos answer a scene or tour a map and name no culprit. Test: the Indonesia long-form names who rewrote the story; around 22 November compare its subscribers per 1,000 with the Asia long-form's.
- Long-form views fell 38.1% and watch time 41.3% week over week to 2026-11-16, with a median average view of 29.8%. Probable cause: the Asia long-form's Home-feed run ending, not a new fault; the Indonesia launch is not in those days. Test: the week to 23 November, which has the launch in it.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-16. Long-form is a Home-feed channel: 150,112 long-form views over 28 days came from the bucket that holds Home and the subscriptions feed, against 4,099 from search. Engaged views were 40.4% of long-form views over 90 days, so a view now counts for less than it did before August.
- The Indonesia long-form is drawing viewers from the country it is about: comments from Indonesia and Java, one from a Muslim in Java who grew up with the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, and one saying corrections are needed. That audience is what the Bali follow-up is for.
- Most new subscribers click on the channel page, not under a video: 854 subscribers gained over 28 days carried no content type, against 477 net from all uploads. Community posts brought 2 on 366,473 views; posts buy views, not subscribers.
- Shorts drew 28.6% of their views from search over 28 days, and the finding that search carries the Shorts has fallen out of its range: the film Shorts rode the Shorts feed, 162,535 views over the same 28 days.

## How they are reacting
The Indonesia long-form's comments are now in the data and are the liveliest part of the sample: Indonesians adding to it and correcting it, Indian viewers angry at the rewriting, and new viewers saying they subscribed. Under the Asia long-form the most-liked objection is still the Chola fleet.
- **Indonesians answering back** (positive): "Watching this hit close to home because we are living through the exact implications of what you just explained."
- **A correction from Indonesia** (mixed): "its great video but few correction probably needed. Rama were never worshiped in Classical Nusantara (present day countries describe as malay archipelago) esp. in the Majapahit era"
- **Anger at the rewriting** (negative): "Distortion of our scriptures"
- **New viewers subscribing** (positive): "Now I know it all started with Parameswara wanting successful trade. Great video, subscribed"
- **The Chola objection to the Asia long-form** (negative): "“Never sent a single soldier…” ever heard of Chola Empire?"
- **Requests for Hindi** (neutral): "Vai, aap hindi mee bhi video banao na. English mee problem hota hya"

Requested topics
- Rajendra Chola's fleet to Srivijaya, the most-liked objection under the Asia long-form
- Bagan in Myanmar, the next most-liked
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one
- Hindi versions of the long-forms

## Competitors
The watchlist is still mostly reacting to the film. Two outliers this month show openings worth borrowing for the Bali long-form, and one is a gap Itiha has a draft for.
- **The Emissary**: "Why Did Japan Make Indian Propaganda Posters?"
  Why it worked: 548,962 views at 15x the channel's median. It opens on an object on screen (“Check out these posters from India's freedom struggle. Japan made them.”) and asks why in the third sentence.
  Steal: Open on a thing the viewer can see, then the question. For Bali: a temple or a manuscript on screen, and the question of why it survived in the next line.
- **Project SHIVOHAM**: "She's NOT Subhadra? The Forgotten Ancient Goddess"
  Why it worked: 261,290 views at 10x, a long-form. It opens on a picture millions hold (the three deities at Puri), gives the accepted answer, then doubts it in the third sentence.
  Steal: The same order for Bali: the picture everyone holds of the Hindu island, the accepted explanation, then the turn.

Gaps
- Why Japan backed India's freedom fight: The Emissary's Short has no match in Itiha's catalogue, and the Rash Behari Bose long-form draft, on its third version on disk, covers the same alliance.
- Where Hinduism survived in Indonesia: the next question the Indonesia long-form's own viewers raise.

## Trending now, make this
- **today, short, 3/5**: Tipu Sultan, 20 November: due tomorrow, nothing scripted  
  Signal: Owner's pick of 15 November; the radar's step this week is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “tipu sultan history”. His birth date is disputed and the Karnataka row is out of the news. (Moments radar, owner's note)  
  Make: Decision 1: script and record today, publish 20 November before 18:00 IST, judge on 23 November. If it cannot ship by 22 November, drop it and give the time to Tegh Bahadur.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Guru Tegh Bahadur, 24 November  
  Signal: The top-ranked dated moment, five days out, titled with the searched name “guru tegh bahadur history”. What it rests on: the date. Mughal and persecution Shorts without a film behind them have landed at or below the usual over the last six months. (Moments radar, calendar)  
  Make: Decision 2: script by 21 November, record on 22, publish the evening of 23 November, judge on 26. Sentence one is Aurangzeb's order, the place and the date.
- **watch, short, 2/5**: Tarabai jails her own king, 24 November 1750  
  Signal: On the radar for the same day as Tegh Bahadur, from a lower-confidence date source. The channel's Tarabai Short against Aurangzeb is one of its four breakouts. (Moments radar, own breakouts)  
  Make: Not on this date: Tegh Bahadur has 24 November and one Short a day is the limit. Keep it as a later Short, the sequel to that breakout (see ideas).
- **watch, short, 3/5**: Winston Churchill's birthday, 30 November  
  Signal: The radar asks this week whether the date carries a long-form; its next step is due 23 November. (Moments radar)  
  Make: Not a long-form: the Bali long-form has that slot. Decide on 23 November; if Tegh Bahadur has shipped, one Short on a single documented act against India. No proof either way on this channel: its one Churchill Short lost viewers in its first seconds to background about the INA.
- **today, skip, 1/5**: Rani Lakshmibai and Indira Gandhi on X today  
  Signal: Both birthdays are trending on X in India today. (X trends, calendar)  
  Make: Skip. A freedom-fighter biography and a recent prime minister are the two kinds of Short that have done below the usual here, and posting on the day itself has failed before.
- **watch, skip, 3/5**: The Great Famine of 1876 to 1878 on Wikipedia  
  Signal: English readership at 5.22x its 30-day median. (Wikipedia pageviews)  
  Make: Skip a remake: you already made it, as the Madras famine Short on Temple's wage, published 18 October.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [3/5, long] **Why Bali Is Still Hindu: The Priests Who Left Java**  
  Identity and religion stakes: the one island in Indonesia that stayed Hindu; Empire mechanism: the conquest that ended Majapahit; Hidden history: the other half of the Indonesia story  
  source: Decision 3. The topic is a guess from the Indonesia long-form's comments; the title is a guess too.
- [3/5, long] **Rajendra Chola's Fleet: The Time India Did Send an Army**  
  Empire mechanism: who controlled the sea route to China; Nation stakes; Contested history: own viewers dispute the Asia long-form's “never sent a single soldier”  
  source: Most-liked objection under the Asia long-form. Rests on the comments, not on any result; a candidate after Bali, not before.
- [2/5, short] **The Queen Who Saved the Swarajya Then Jailed Its King**  
  Villain plus hypocrisy: the regent who held off Aurangzeb imprisoned her own Chhatrapati; Hidden history: what Tarabai did after the war  
  source: Moments radar, 24 November 1750. A sequel to the channel's Tarabai breakout, but that one came in the Chhava film window; without a film it is a guess.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,466 followers, up 247 in 7 days, 35.3 a day. The latest reel, “Every Ramayan kept one rule. The New Namit Malhotra film broke it.”, reached 12,107 with a skip rate of 40.5% against a reel median of 54.1%. Carousels remain the growth format at 3.74x the median reach of reels.

Do more
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 37 followers (90 posts); outside the band, 12 (15 posts). Pooled rate 2.97 vs 1.88 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 385 followers a month at stake.
- Write carousels in the revision lane  
  51 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53 followers against 22 for the other lanes (39 posts). Median reach 15.3k vs 12.5k, conversion 3.77 vs 2.12 per 1k. 357 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  19 of 103 rated posts are shared above the median (25.7/1k) but convert below it (2.2/1k): median 12.8k reach for a median 12 followers. The 33 posts that do both average 283 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 956 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  87 single images all time: 83.1k reach between them and 118 followers, 1.4 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 157.2. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 91 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **now**: Reply to the Indonesian viewer who says corrections are needed under “Why Ravana Gets His Powers From ALLAH in This Ramayana”: say what the video got right and what it should have said. /replies drafts it.  
  It is a correction from the country in the story, under a video that is climbing, so new viewers read it. That a reply helps is a guess, not a measured effect.
- **this_week**: If not done yet, put the Indonesia long-form on the end screen and in the pinned comment of “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?”.  
  The Asia long-form has 156,794 views, the largest long-form audience the channel has, and the same subject.
- **this_week**: Make the Indonesia long-form the channel page's featured video for visitors who have not subscribed, while it climbs.  
  854 subscribers over 28 days came from the channel page rather than any video. That the featured video moves them is a guess.
- **this_week**: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” has 0 views since 3 November, and the two Shorts published with it, “Itihasa vs Myth” (82) and “Is Caste Unique to India?” (255).  
  A public Short gets at least a handful of views, so no views at all points to its visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.
- **later**: Add the Google Analytics property number to the settings file.  
  Without it the brief cannot say how itiha.info is doing, so the website is left out today.
